topic.title: Painting Project
topic.description: Extracts a color palette from an image using the colorgram library and recreates it as a dot painting with turtle. Combines external libraries with turtle graphics.

learningNotes.whatILearned: A dot painting: a turtle lays coloured dots across the canvas in a grid, each row starting further left.
learningNotes.challenges: I cannot run it here, and neither can you — there is no tkinter on this machine or on Termux.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Get a Python with tkinter onto a machine with a screen, and read the colourgram part: that is where the real idea is.

files.description: Dot painting with colors extracted from an image.

misconceptions: `colorgram` reads the colours out of an image file - the dots are then painted in colours taken from that image
A turtle that lays dots and moves on is a different tool from a turtle that draws lines - `dot()` fills, `forward()` draws
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 25 + 5 = 30%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter`. The 40 points for *it runs* are
therefore not points I can give, and I do not give them.

The larger point: **`tkinter` does not exist on Termux either.** These
files cannot be run on the phone this whole system is built around. They
are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

The idea is the famous one and the code matches it. `colormode(255)` lets the colours be three numbers from 0 to 255, `color_list` is a list of 26 such RGB triples, and the loop lays 100 dots of size 20 with a random colour from the list, moving 50 units between them. Every tenth dot the turtle turns 90 degrees, steps down 50, turns again, and steps back 500 — which is what makes the rows line up as a grid instead of a single long line.

`main.py` in the same topic is a smaller version of the same thing: it makes the colour list, makes a turtle, draws one big red dot and stops. It is the first step of the project, kept next to the finished one.

**What is not**

The interesting half of the project is commented out at the top of the file — the `colorgram` block that reads the colours out of an actual image. That block is the *point* of the exercise: the whole design is *take the colours from a picture, then paint a picture made of those colours*. With the block commented out, the file paints random colours from a hand-written list, which is a different (and much easier) program.

The comment at the top does say this — *This code will not work in repl.it as there is no access to the colorgram package here* — but the honest consequence is not spelled out: **the file as it stands cannot do the thing it is named after.** It needs an image file that is not in the archive, and a package that is not installed.

**The one thing to fix first**

Get an image and the package, then the commented block becomes the program:

```python
import colorgram

rgb_colors = [(c.rgb.r, c.rgb.g, c.rgb.b) for c in colorgram.extract('image.jpg', 30)]
```

Then the dot loop uses `rgb_colors` instead of the hand-written list, and the painting is made of the colours in your photograph.
